//: Firestore indexes, as code.
Every query the app makes today is a single-field orderBy on a subcollection,
which Firestore indexes automatically — so nothing here is required to make
the current product work. This file exists so that the first query that DOES
need an index arrives with the index in the same commit, rather than as a
production error telling someone to click a link in a console.
Timing matters more than it looks: building a composite index backfills the
whole collection. Declaring one now, while these collections are empty, is
effectively free. Declaring it after a year of watcher runs is an outage.
The Watchers screen lists runs for one watcher, newest first. listRuns()
currently orders across all watchers, so this is not yet exercised — but
filtering by watcherId while ordering by anything other than watcherId is
exactly the shape Firestore refuses without a composite.
The Feedback Ledger, filtered to one session. FR-V5 records what was
confirmed, declined and corrected; reading back one session's decisions
is the query that view needs.
sessions.plan is an array of step objects. Firestore indexes every element
of an array field by default, so a four-step plan costs four index entries
per write — for a field nothing ever queries or orders by. The exemption
turns that off.
This is a write-cost and latency saving, not a correctness fix: leaving it
on would work, just wastefully, and the waste scales with plan length.
Verification codes are write-once and read once, within ten minutes.
Nothing queries them by createdAt — the code is fetched by document id —
so the automatic index is pure overhead. The TTL policy in Terraform is
what deletes them; this only stops us paying to index the field meanwhile.
